uncited: **Covariance Regularization:** To prevent aliasing (high-frequency artifacts) when zooming out or rendering at low resolution, a low-pass filter is applied.
**Opacity Preservation:** Adding variance spreads the Gaussian, reducing its peak height.
**Frequency Matching:** The filter parameters are tuned to match the Nyquist limit of the rendering resolution.
For training-time methods, this involves constraining the 3D representation frequency to the training data's sampling rate.
MIP-Splatting was introduced to address these resolution-dependent artifacts by integrating multi-scale representations.
Subsequent works like SA-GS and FilterGS expanded the family to include test-time adaptations and performance optimizations.
